notes: Tudor paternal line intentionally not modeled. Founder of the Tudor royal line in this tree. Born at Pembroke Castle in Wales on 28 January 1457; only child of Margaret Beaufort (aged 13) and Edmund Tudor, who died before his birth.

deathCause.detail: Henry VII died at Richmond Palace of tuberculosis, after declining health; no violent cause is recorded.
deathCause.detailCn: 亨利七世在健康恶化后因肺结核去世于里士满宫；无暴力死因记载。

events.label: Battle of Bosworth Field
events.note: Henry defeated and killed Richard III on 22 August 1485, ending the Wars of the Roses.

events.label: Became King of England
events.note: Henry claimed the crown on the field of battle by right of conquest, backdated to 21 August 1485; Parliament confirmed his title in November 1485.

events.label: Coronation as King of England
events.note: Crowned at Westminster Abbey on 30 October 1485.

events.label: Marriage to Elizabeth of York
events.labelCn: 与约克的伊丽莎白成婚
events.note: Married Elizabeth of York at Westminster Abbey on 18 January 1486, uniting the Houses of Lancaster and York and securing Yorkist acceptance of his reign.

events.label: Battle of Stoke Field
events.note: Final battle of the Wars of the Roses: Yorkist rebels backing the pretender Lambert Simnel were crushed and John de la Pole, Earl of Lincoln, was killed.

events.label: Treaty of Medina del Campo
events.note: Signed in March 1489 with Spain; betrothed Arthur, Prince of Wales, to Catherine of Aragon.

events.label: Treaty of Etaples
events.note: Signed on 3 November 1492 after Henry's brief invasion of France; Charles VIII paid a large indemnity and agreed not to shelter pretenders.

events.label: Intercursus Magnus with Burgundy
events.labelCn: 与勃艮第签订《大通商条约》
events.note: Signed in February 1496; restored the wool and cloth trade with the Burgundian Netherlands after the trade embargo.

events.label: Perkin Warbeck's rising in Cornwall
events.labelCn: 珀金·沃贝克在康沃尔登陆起事
events.note: Warbeck, who claimed to be Richard of York (one of the Princes in the Tower), landed in Cornwall in September 1497 and was quickly captured; he was executed in 1499.

events.label: Death of Arthur, Prince of Wales
events.note: Arthur died at Ludlow Castle on 2 April 1502, very likely of the sweating sickness, making the future Henry VIII the heir.

events.label: Margaret Tudor weds James IV of Scotland
events.labelCn: 长女玛格丽特与苏格兰詹姆斯四世联姻
events.note: Margaret married James IV on 8 August 1503 under the Treaty of Perpetual Peace (1502); the match later carried the Stuart claim to the English throne.

events.label: Death of Henry VII
events.note: Henry died at Richmond Palace of tuberculosis on 21 April 1509 and was succeeded by his son Henry VIII.

notes: Only the Mary I and Elizabeth I branches are modeled here; his six wives and his other children (including Edward VI) remain outside this pass, so marriages are covered as events rather than as relationship links.

deathCause.detail: Henry VIII died at Whitehall Palace after years of serious health problems, including severe leg ulcers, a gangrenous leg wound from a 1536 jousting accident, and declining mobility; the exact cause of death is uncertain.
deathCause.detailCn: 亨利八世在多年严重健康问题后于白厅宫去世，包括严重的腿部溃疡、1536年比武事故造成的腿部坏疽以及行动能力衰退；确切死因尚无定论。

events.label: Became King of England
events.note: Succeeded on the death of his father Henry VII on 21 April 1509.

events.label: Marriage to Catherine of Aragon
events.labelCn: 与阿拉贡的凯瑟琳成婚
events.note: Married Catherine, widow of his elder brother Arthur, at Greenwich on 11 June 1509; they were crowned together on 24 June.

events.label: Coronation as King of England
events.note: Crowned at Westminster Abbey together with Catherine of Aragon on 24 June 1509.

events.label: The King's Great Matter begins
events.labelCn: “国王的大事”——亨利谋求废除与凯瑟琳的婚姻
events.note: Henry sought the annulment of his marriage to Catherine of Aragon, citing her earlier marriage to Arthur; the Pope's refusal set the course towards the break with Rome.

events.label: Marriage to Anne Boleyn
events.note: Secret marriage to the pregnant Anne Boleyn in London; Cranmer's court declared the Catherine marriage void on 23 May 1533.

events.label: Annulment of marriage to Catherine of Aragon
events.labelCn: 宣布与阿拉贡的凯瑟琳的婚姻无效
events.note: Archbishop Cranmer's court at Dunstable declared the marriage to Catherine invalid; Catherine never accepted the ruling.

events.label: Birth of Elizabeth I
events.labelCn: 伊丽莎白（后来的伊丽莎白一世）出生
events.note: Anne Boleyn gave birth to Elizabeth at Greenwich Palace on 7 September 1533; Henry's disappointment over a daughter weakened Anne's position.

events.label: Act of Supremacy
events.note: The First Act of Supremacy (royal assent 3 November 1534) declared Henry Supreme Head of the Church of England; Pope Clement VII's excommunication of Henry was not made official until later.

events.label: Execution of Anne Boleyn
events.note: Anne was beheaded on Tower Green on 19 May 1536 after conviction for treason and adultery on charges widely regarded as engineered.

events.label: Dissolution of the Monasteries begins
events.note: The First Suppression Act (1536) closed the smaller religious houses; the Second Suppression Act (1539) dissolved the rest, with their wealth and lands seized by the Crown.

events.label: Pilgrimage of Grace
events.note: A major northern rising, begun in October 1536, against the dissolution of the monasteries and religious changes; its leaders were pardoned and then executed in 1537.

events.label: Birth of Edward VI
events.labelCn: 爱德华（后来的爱德华六世）出生
events.note: Jane Seymour bore the long-awaited male heir on 12 October 1537; she died of complications on 24 October 1537.

events.label: Marriage to Anne of Cleves
events.labelCn: 与克利夫斯的安妮成婚
events.note: Political marriage sealed on the strength of a Holbein portrait; the marriage was never consummated and was annulled on 9 July 1540.

events.label: Annulment of marriage to Anne of Cleves
events.labelCn: 宣布与克利夫斯的安妮的婚姻无效
events.note: Annulled on grounds of non-consummation and an alleged pre-contract; Anne accepted a generous settlement and outlived Henry.

events.label: Became King of Ireland
events.note: Crown of Ireland Act: passed by the Irish Parliament in 1541, with royal assent following in 1542; the event is dated per the original record.

events.label: Death of Henry VIII
events.note: Henry died at Whitehall Palace on 28 January 1547 after years of declining health and was succeeded by Edward VI.

notes: Daughter of Henry VIII; her mother Catherine of Aragon is intentionally not modeled in this pass. Died during an influenza epidemic; modern scholars suspect ovarian cysts or uterine cancer. 'Bloody Mary' is a posthumous epithet tied to the Marian persecutions.

deathCause.detail: Mary died at St James's Palace on 17 November 1558, aged 42, during an influenza epidemic; modern scholars suspect ovarian cysts or uterine cancer as the underlying cause. Not a violent death.
deathCause.detailCn: 玛丽于1558年11月17日在圣詹姆斯宫去世，享年42岁，正值流感流行期间；现代学者推测潜在死因可能是卵巢囊肿或子宫癌。非暴力死亡。

events.label: Birth of Mary at Greenwich Palace
events.labelCn: 玛丽在格林尼治宫出生
events.note: Only child of Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon to survive infancy.

events.label: Declared illegitimate and removed from succession
events.labelCn: 被宣告为私生女并排除出继承序列
events.note: In May 1533 Cranmer annulled Henry VIII's marriage to Catherine of Aragon; Mary was deemed illegitimate, styled 'The Lady Mary' and barred from the succession.

events.label: Restored to succession by the Third Succession Act
events.labelCn: 经《第三次继承法》恢复继承权
events.note: Henry VIII placed Mary after Edward in the line of succession, though she remained legally illegitimate.

events.label: Wyatt's Rebellion in Kent
events.note: January-February 1554: revolt led by Thomas Wyatt the Younger against Mary's planned marriage to Philip of Spain; suppressed in February, Wyatt executed.

events.label: Restoration of Papal Supremacy
events.note: Existing event, dated: 30 November 1554 Cardinal Pole absolved Parliament in Mary's presence, ending the English schism with Rome.

events.label: Marian Persecutions begin (c. 280 burned)
events.labelCn: 玛丽宗教迫害开始（约280人被处火刑）
events.note: First burnings in February 1555; more than 280 Protestants were executed by burning by 1558. Factual record, kept neutral.

events.label: Loss of Calais to France
events.note: Existing event, dated: French forces took Calais in January 1558 (capitulation 7 January), England's last continental possession.

fullNameCn: 英格兰女王伊丽莎白一世
notes: Daughter of Henry VIII; her mother Anne Boleyn is intentionally not modeled in this pass. Last Tudor monarch. Never married, and died without issue; she was succeeded by James VI of Scotland.

deathCause.detail: Elizabeth died at Richmond Palace on 24 March 1603 after a period of declining health in the final months of her reign; the immediate cause of death is uncertain.
deathCause.detailCn: 伊丽莎白在其统治的最后数月健康状况持续衰退，于1603年3月24日在里士满宫去世；直接死因尚无定论。

events.label: Imprisoned in the Tower of London
events.labelCn: 因怀亚特叛乱受嫌被囚于伦敦塔
events.note: Suspected of involvement in Wyatt's Rebellion, Elizabeth was imprisoned in the Tower on 18 March 1554 and later held at Woodstock; she was released in 1555.

events.label: Became Queen of England
events.note: Elizabeth succeeded on the death of her half-sister Mary I on 17 November 1558.

events.label: Coronation as Queen of England
events.note: Crowned at Westminster Abbey on 15 January 1559.

events.label: Elizabethan Religious Settlement
events.note: The Act of Supremacy (law from 8 May 1559) restored the royal supremacy and the Act of Uniformity established the 1559 Book of Common Prayer, defining the Protestant Church of England.

events.label: Poor Act of 1563
events.note: Early poor-relief legislation; further Acts followed in 1598 and 1601.

events.label: Mary, Queen of Scots flees to England
events.labelCn: 苏格兰女王玛丽逃入英格兰并被软禁
events.note: After her defeat at Langside in May 1568, Mary fled to England and was detained for nineteen years, becoming the focus of Catholic plots.

events.label: Papal excommunication of Elizabeth
events.labelCn: 教皇颁布诏书绝罚伊丽莎白
events.note: Pope Pius V issued Regnans in Excelsis on 25 February 1570, excommunicating Elizabeth and absolving English Catholics of allegiance to her.

events.label: Courtship of Francis, Duke of Anjou
events.labelCn: 安茹公爵弗朗索瓦的求婚
events.note: The last serious marriage negotiation; the courtship collapsed by 1581 and Elizabeth remained unmarried — the 'Virgin Queen'.

events.label: Treaty of Nonsuch with the Dutch
events.labelCn: 与荷兰签订《楠萨奇条约》
events.note: England pledged military support to the Dutch Revolt on 20 August 1585, provoking the Anglo-Spanish War.

events.label: Execution of Mary, Queen of Scots
events.note: Mary was beheaded at Fotheringhay Castle on 8 February 1587 after the Babington Plot; Elizabeth claimed the signed warrant had been sent without her knowledge.

events.label: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
events.note: The Spanish Armada sailed in July 1588; English fire-ships scattered it off Gravelines on 28-29 July, and storms wrecked many of the surviving ships on the Irish coast.

events.label: Essex's Rebellion
events.note: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, led a failed rising in London on 8 February 1601 and was executed on 25 February.

events.label: Elizabethan Poor Law
events.note: The 1601 Elizabethan Poor Law consolidated earlier legislation (1563, 1598) and shaped English poor relief for centuries.

events.label: The Golden Speech
events.note: Elizabeth's farewell speech to Parliament on 30 November 1601, affirming her bond with her subjects.

events.label: Death of Elizabeth I
events.note: Elizabeth died at Richmond Palace on 24 March 1603; James VI of Scotland succeeded as James I, ending the Tudor dynasty.

fullNameCn: 英格兰国王爱德华六世

events.label: Second Book of Common Prayer introduced

deathCause.detail: Edward VI died at Greenwich Palace on 6 July 1553 after a long illness, probably tuberculosis.
deathCause.detailCn: 1553年7月6日，爱德华六世在长期患病后于格林尼治宫去世，可能死于肺结核。

sourceNote: Only son of Henry VIII to survive infancy; succeeded by Mary I after the short Lady Jane Grey episode. Core chronology completed 2026-08-20.
notes: Basic main-line succession card; mother Jane Seymour is outside the current roster.
